text: The year was 1893, and the last natural forest on Earth was a spectacle that many traveled miles to behold. Eli, a young botanist, stood in awe among the ancient trees, a leather-bound journal in hand as he recorded notes about species that had become legends. This sacred grove, unbeknownst to him, was about to become the centerpiece of a historic preservation effort that would challenge the industrial metropolis encroaching upon the natural world. The city of Paris, known for the Eiffel Tower, loomed in the distance, its iron skeleton a stark contrast to the organic chaos of the woods.
